title: Positive Influence as a Positive Bias Change
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ be monotone in the coordinatewise order, and let $J\\subseteq\\{0,\\ldots,n-1\\}$. Write $f_{J,+}$ for the function obtained by setting every coordinate in $J$ to $+1$ before applying $f$, and write the positive bias of a function for the uniform probability that its value is $+1$. Then the coalitional influence of $f$ toward $+1$ equals the positive bias of $f_{J,+}$ minus the positive bias of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the sign cube to the signs
